title: twilight-oncall-log-mina-2028-06-18
content:
TWILIGHT SHIFT NOTES (Mina) — 2028-06-18

Overview / mood: slow start, small flurry at 02:13 UTC, then steady. Good run aside from one noisy page about model-serving tail latency. Lots of small follow-ups; this doc is my scratchpad for actions, commands, and half-formed troubleshooting notes.

Timeline (quick):
- 01:48 UTC — pager: embedding-worker-rt high p50->p99 spike observed by synthetic-canary (us-west2). Alert auto-escalated.
- 02:05 UTC — identified a connection backlog on pgbouncer (dedicated-infer-pool-3).
- 02:22 UTC — applied soft-restart of pgbouncer on pool-3; latency recovered, canary green at 02:30 UTC.
- 04:40 UTC — minor drift alert: autoscaler executed unexpected scale-down on model-serving-65b; manual rollback to min=2 replicas.

Immediate incident summary:
- Symptom: transient tokenization/embedding requests high latency (p50 normal, p95/p99 spiking).
- Root cause (hypothesis): pgbouncer connection pool exhaustion + short-lived upstream retry storm from client SDK v1.7.2 that bursts connections (see ENGOPS-4827).
- Mitigation taken: soft restart pgbouncer on the affected node group (command below), adjusted pool size + enabled connection-lifetime jitter in config. Rolled a small agent patch to reject new SDK v1.7.2 connections for now via header-based policy in edge-rates.
- Status: resolved for now; monitoring for recurrence.

Commands / notes (copyable):
- Check pgbouncer backlog: sudo systemctl status pgbouncer@pool-3 && tail -n 100 /var/log/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.log
- Soft-restart (no downtime): sudo -u postgres pgbouncer -R -d /etc/pgbouncer/pool-3.ini  # (confirmed safe on 02:20 UTC)
- Bump pool size (temporary): edit /etc/pgbouncer/pool-3.ini set max_client_conn=1200 -> 1600; sudo systemctl reload pgbouncer@pool-3

Evidence snippets (copied from logs):
- "[02:11:14] WARNING: denied connection: too many clients (current=1034, max=1000)"
- "sdk-client v=1.7.2: rapid reconnects from 10.23.45.77:42218 -> 350/5m"

Follow-ups / action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Mina: file postmortem note in ENGOPS-4827 (first draft by 2028-06-19 EOD) — include timeline, pgbouncer metrics, and SDK mitigation.
- Luca: add integration test for SDK reconnect churn on staging (Jenkins job) — due 2028-06-24.
- Harper: update runbook pgbouncer.md with soft-restart procedure and config knobs we changed — due 2028-06-20.
- Platform-Infra: evaluate replacing pgbouncer w/ managed pooler for dedicated pools (RFC) — assignee TBD; add to infra roadmap.

Runbook TODOs (explicit checklist; convert into runbook PR):
- [ ] Add section: "identifying connection exhaustion vs backend slowness" (include queries to Grafana panels).
- [x] Documented soft-restart technique (committed to notes but need to PR runbook) — partial.
- [ ] Add snippet: how to toggle edge header-based rejects for SDK v1.7.x (safelist vs blocklist examples).
- [ ] Create alert suppression guide for scheduled pgbouncer maintenance windows.

Open questions / assumptions to verify:
- Is SDK v1.7.2 widespread in customers or just a few internal bots? (check telemetry by client_version tag)
- When pgbouncer hits max_client_conn, do we want to fail fast or queue longer? Current setting is fail-fast (was useful historically). Might be worth revisiting for embedding workloads where short queues are fine.
- Did autoscaler scale-down happen because of stale metrics? Need to trace the datapipeline from model-serving metrics to HPA decision. See INFRA-2110.

Paging notes (what I wrote to the channel / handoff text):
- Posted summary to #sre: "02:12 UTC — pgbouncer pool-3 connection backlog, soft restart applied, monitoring. Follow-ups: runbook update + SDK triage (ENGOPS-4827)."
- DM to oncall-eng-sre rotation lead to mention potential change to alert thresholds if this repeats.

Personal quick todo (post shift):
- Sleep.
- Draft the postmortem skeleton w/ data pulls (pgbouncer cpu/mem, connection graphs, client_version histogram).
- Add to calendar: pair with Luca on 6/22 for staging test design.

Nice-to-have notes / ideas (brainstorm):
- Smart-queueing: a lightweight queue in front of pgbouncer that provides token-bucket smoothing for bursts coming from SDK (trade-offs: latency vs retries).
- Rework our client SDK to include backoff jitter serverside header that tells edge to smooth reconnects. Could be a short-term negotiated extension.

Oddities observed (may be noise):
- A few spikes correlated with one client IP range that belongs to an internal load-testing job — need to confirm with platform-tests team.
- Small number of 502s from edge when pool was saturated; unknown if that was client or ambassador proxy behavior.

Links/refs to include in postmortem:
- JIRA ENGOPS-4827 (incident ticket)
- INFRA-2110 (autoscaler drift investigation)
- github PR #1289 (edge header-based reject rule)

End-of-shift handoff blurb (to paste into rotation doc):
- "Resolved transient pgbouncer connection exhaustion affecting embedding workers. Soft restart applied; added temporary pool size increase and header-based mitigation for SDK v1.7.2. Monitoring stable. Follow-ups: runbook updates (Harper), staging reconnect test (Luca), postmortem doc (Mina)."

Random scratch reminders (for me):
- Look up who owns the internal load-test job (I think it's platform-tests/team: pipeline-qa).
- Check whether dedicated pool-3 has a cron job that rotates certs at 02:00 (could explain connection churn).

-- Mina
